title: 15th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened with the usual business: minutes of earlier sittings were accepted, two committee seat changes were announced, and a question to the Foreign Minister was put off at his request. The chair sent the President's request to extend the Children's Ombudsperson's term to the Human Rights and Gender Committee. The main item was the first-stage debate on the government's Trademark Bill, brought by Maduvvari MP Ahmed Zahir. Most speakers backed it as protection for Maldivian creators and businesses, while some said enforcement of existing laws, Dhivehi wording and overlap with copyright law needed attention. The debate was paused with members still on the speaking list absent, and the sitting ended.

items.title: Introduction of the Trademark Bill (government, sponsored by Ahmed Zahir, Maduvvari)
Preliminary debate on the Trademark Bill
items.outcome: debated by 14 members; paused for lack of further speakers present, to continue at a later sitting

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: As sponsor, said the bill creates trademark registration and court remedies for misuse, including fines of MVR 100,000 to 2 million, and asked members to improve it.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Welcomed the first-ever trademark bill as important for the digital economy and hoped committee stage would consult stakeholders.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Backed the bill as a way to protect young Maldivian artisans' work and brands, and urged expert input at committee.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill, saying registered brands protect businesses and entrepreneurs and show products are Maldivian when sold abroad.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill as overdue and asked that artisans' and experts' views be gathered at committee stage.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Regretted the bill has no Dhivehi name and said fading traditional crafts need protection; asked for changes at committee.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Offered condolences for the previous night's accident, supported the bill, and said it comes at a time when brands of long-running businesses are being lost.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said laws also need enforcement and local products need export routes; noted souvenirs sold in shops are largely imported.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said he would not support the bill, arguing existing copyright law already covers the ground and a new law may overlap with other laws.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Raised concern over the 'exclusive right' wording and the bill being drafted in English, and called for drafting in Dhivehi.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said he received the bill only the day before; argued enforcement matters more than new laws; spoke about workers' rights and wages.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said trademarks separate originals from fakes, and questioned the Foreign Minister's deferral of his question under the 14-day rule.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Supported the bill, suggested sound marks be covered, and said patent and trade-secret laws are also needed alongside it.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Offered condolences, raised road and ferry accidents in Greater Malé, and noted overlap between this bill and the copyright bill to be fixed at committee.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 9 to 11 were accepted as no amendments were proposed.
Committee seat changes announced: Mohamed Mamdooh to Judiciary Committee, Mauroof Zakir to Social Committee.
Question 6.1 to the Foreign Minister deferred at his request.
Presidential request on the Children's Ombudsperson's term sent to the Human Rights and Gender Committee.
Trademark Bill given its first reading and preliminary debate; debate paused, to continue at a later sitting.
Next sitting set for 15 July 2025 at 9:00.
